export const meta = {
  name: 'globe-writers-2',
  description: 'Rewrite the plan sections 1-7 for the website and write the architecture, open-questions and shared-prerequisites sections as fragments',
  phases: [{ title: 'Write', detail: 'plan writer and architecture writer in parallel' }],
}

const REPO = '/home/user/RoofingApp'
const EVID = REPO + '/research/globe/validation-evidence/'
const SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad'
const FRAG = SCRATCH + '/readme-sections/'

const CTX = `You are a section writer for research/globe/README.md, the single reference document for the "3D storm view" (globe) research in RoofingApp. A supervisor assembles the sections; write ONLY your fragment file(s), in Markdown, nothing else. Never modify README.md itself.

Read first, in this order: ${EVID}main-architecture.json (the product is now the Montana Hail Watch WEBSITE: static pages built every 10 minutes by GitHub Actions and published on Pages; the browser may fetch only site files; third-party code is vendored, never a CDN; phones first; its 24 "what the globe plan must change" points), ${EVID}design-synthesis-website.json (the recommended hybrid, decisions to write D30+, owner decisions OW-1…, phases with numeric gates, dissent), ${EVID}design-d.json (the website globe design: three.js, bytes, JS duties, owner decisions O-2…O-15, phases), ${EVID}judge2-rules.json, judge2-engineering.json, judge2-product.json (scores and grafts), ${SCRATCH}/supervisor-log.md (the supervisor's verdicts: the ACCEPT/REJECT lists for the two plan critiques, the architecture shift, the refuter verdicts, the prototype findings), ${SCRATCH}/plan-critique-product.json and plan-critique-technical.json (the critiques), ${REPO}/research/globe/README.md sections 1-7 (the ORIGINAL plan, written for the parked desktop app — you are replacing it; keep what still holds, especially the evidence rules), the fragments already written in ${FRAG} (08-sources.md, 09a-rendering.md, 10-pipeline.md — do not repeat their content; cross-reference their section numbers), and the evidence files you cite. In every evidence file a "review" key wins over "facts"; mark "unreviewed" where there is none.

The supervisor's standing instructions: the owner (Carson) asked for "a version of Google Earth with holographic imagery for clouds and storms" and said the plan is for him to decide on; present his choices plainly rather than deciding for him; the agents' recommendation (the hybrid) and the direct route (design D now) both appear with costs; "holographic" is kept as his word for the goal and the UI name is a decision; no "best" claims (AGENTS.md rule 9); evidence honesty wording (rule 5); the site's gap words and states; every number carries a unit and a source link to its evidence file, e.g. [mrms.json](validation-evidence/mrms.json), or "computed: <formula>"; unverified items are written "unverified" with why; never write model names or AI-vendor identifiers; house style: plain wording, sentence case, direct and brief, tables and ranked lists over prose, no emoji. Headings exactly "## N. Title" with the numbers given; subsections "###". Stay within the line budget. Return as your final text: the fragment path(s), line counts, the evidence files cited, and any contradiction you found between files.`

const A = `# Fragment: sections 1-7 → ${FRAG}01-plan.md (budget 280 lines)
Replace the original plan's sections 1-7 for the website. Structure:
Title line "# 3D storm view (globe) — research scaffold" then a status paragraph: date 2026-10-17; branch codex/montana-weather-pilot merged with main at 195d68c (the product is now the website, D27); research only, nothing ships (merging to main publishes the site — nothing here touches website/); the branch carries pull request #2 (an earlier Montana pilot) so the globe files could be moved to a fresh branch from main if preferred; what the sections are and that every fact in 8 onward names its evidence file.
## 1. Bottom line — numbered, 8-10 points: what was asked; what it is in the website's terms (a page or layers built by the 10-minute job; clouds as a satellite picture and an estimated cloud-top height; storms as MRMS reflectivity volumes; all data hosted by the site); the two routes side by side — (a) the staged route the agents recommend (storm layers on the existing Map page first: text, Band 13 picture, echo-top raster, loop; a link-only three.js globe gated at the synthesis's P4 and an owner approval) and (b) the direct route (design D's globe page now) — each with first-visit bytes, build bytes, JS lines, what it delivers of the ask, and what must be relaxed; the hard limit: the site's "browser fetches only site files" rule makes streamed worldwide imagery (the Google Earth look) impossible without decision D-G1, and what a Montana-box globe can still show; data facts that are settled (sources free and reachable; measured sizes); what the prototype proved in a real browser; the pilot/baseline gate from the roadmap; what Carson decides next.
## 2. Decisions Carson needs to make — one table: id (keep D-G1…D-G9 from the original and add D-G10… for the new ones; show the synthesis's OW-n and design D's O-n ids in a column) · decision · options with their costs (bytes, $/month, JS lines, rule changes) · the agents' recommendation (from the synthesis; say "recommended by the synthesis" not "best") · default if no answer.
## 3. Target picture — what the finished view shows, as a table per layer: layer · kind (the website's separation per AGENTS.md: observation / satellite estimate / radar estimate / model / official alert / base map) · source · produced by (build step) · bytes per build and per visit · state words · legend text. Include the base map (Natural Earth + Census), terrain, the Band 13 picture, the cloud-top height deck (phase 2), MRMS volumes, MESH (off until units verified), alerts, the 14 towns, time (what a loop costs). Cite 08-sources.md and 10-pipeline.md.
## 4. Evidence rules applied to the 3D view — keep and tighten the original rules: kinds never merged; no echo is not clear; -99/-999 "no radar data (meanings unverified)"; MRMS heights above mean sea level and the below-ground levels (952 m Billings; 0.5 and 0.75 km levels); cloud top only, never "measured"; the parallax wording from [parallax.json](validation-evidence/parallax.json) quoted verbatim (uncorrected and corrected legends) and the GOES-East grid note; no interpolation between frames or cells; no severity ramps; every hazard colour carries its word; the site's gap words and "This is not an all-clear."; the disclaimer line; the text List; DEMO/sample labelling; exports; the pilot confound.
## 5. Workstreams and what they produced — table W0–W21 (W0 prior work; W1 GIBS; W2 GOES on AWS; W3 MRMS; W4 radar tiles/NEXRAD; W5 terrain; W6 base imagery; W7 globe libraries; W8 WebGL runtime; W9 app integration (desktop-era); W10 Google terms; W11 rendering; W12 pipeline; W13 designs A–D, judges, syntheses; W14 prototype; W15 writers/critic; W16 Montana street-zoom sources; W17 labels over imagery; W18 design references; W19 rights matrix; W20 predeclared evaluation; W21 hosting facts; plus the main-architecture map and parallax) · status · output file(s) · one-line result · what was refuted or corrected.
## 6. Build phases — the synthesis's gates and phases (P0 gates with their numeric conditions; P1–P6 on the Map page; PG the globe) AND design D's direct-route phases 0–5, each with numeric done-when and a stop condition; say which tests and CI steps each needs (test_site additions, test_gridded-style tests, Chromium smoke, width test, path filter).
## 7. Risks, ranked — with the mitigation and the evidence: D-G1 rule; the Actions terms reading (the whole site relies on Actions already); GIBS latency 30–96 min; MRMS -99/-999 unverified; MSL imagery retiring 2026-07-31; WebGL2 on real phones untested; loop bandwidth (12 frames ≈ 10 MB per visit; 2 h at 2-min steps ≈ 217 GB/month against the 100 GB soft limit); honesty traps (dramatic volumes read as damage; exports); pilot confound; JS growth (map.js already 2,155 lines); research/ bytes in the zipball of the parked app; naming/trademark.`

const B = `# Fragments: section 9b → ${FRAG}09b-architecture.md (budget 170 lines); section 14 → ${FRAG}14-questions.md (budget 100 lines); section 15 → ${FRAG}15-prerequisites.md (budget 50 lines)
### 9b. Architecture (continue the "## 9." section that 09a-rendering.md opened; start your fragment with "### 9b. Architecture: where the 3D view lives")
From design-synthesis-website.json, design-d.json, the judge2 files and designs A–C's dissent: the recommended hybrid and why (scores per lens in a table, no "best"); design D in detail (globe.html built by build.py; three.js 0.186.1 MIT 2,120,885 B raw / 417,073 B gzip; MapLibre 6.14.0 as the fallback with its bytes; why CesiumJS is not recommended for the site); the COMPLETE hand-written JavaScript duty list with the one-line reason each must run in the browser and the proposed caps (the synthesis's caps vs design D's 600 lines / 40,000 B — show both and say the owner picks); build additions with bytes per build and per visit; the site-files-only rule and its exception D-G1; alerts with null geometry (zone outline, marker + text, can't-tell), MSL levels below ground, no-data cells, legends; freshness seconds per new source for website/sources.py CONTRACTS (from measured latency: GIBS GOES ~40 min typical, 76–96 min late frames; AWS GOES ~2–3 min; MRMS 2-min source behind a 10-min build); the DECISIONS entries to write (D30–D40 from the synthesis "decisions_to_write", each with its proposed wording in one or two sentences, including the doc-drift fixes: radar 15 vs 30 min; "Folium bundles Leaflet" correction in D23; the website's vendoring precedent); tests and CI; the dissent paragraph (what the losing designs do better and when to prefer them).
## 14. Open questions for Carson
Consolidate and de-duplicate every owner question raised anywhere: the two critiques' questions_for_the_owner, design D's owner decisions O-2…O-15, the synthesis's OW-1…, W20's and parallax.json's open items, the contradictions listed at the end of 08-sources.md and 09a-rendering.md that only he can settle (e.g. 15 vs 30 min radar staleness; whether a 3D view or screenshot may ever reach a homeowner or insurer; crew devices; the OSM Boundary Extractor export format; the Actions terms reading; the name and trademark check; before/after roof imagery as a separate product). Group them: Rules to relax or keep · Product and placement · Data and budget · Honesty and audience · Names and legal. Each question one line, with the decision id it maps to and the section that explains it.
## 15. Prerequisites shared with the site's Map page
Map the product critic's "fix the flat map first" items (plan-critique-product.json honesty_traps and top_5_changes, written for the parked desktop app) onto the website as it is on main (main-architecture.json: page-age banner, gap words, text List, map.js): a table of item · exists on the website today? (file:line from main-architecture.json) · still needed? · where it would go. Include: freshness always visible; a "No radar coverage" state (exists in map.js:33-39 — but the MRMS -99/-999 wording conflict); frame loop with frame times (exists: playback); "no echo is not clear" wording (DESIGN.md:275-276); the disclaimer; "Inspection-confirmed" relabel and the pre-selected hail size (desktop app only — say they do not apply to the site).`

log('Writers-2: plan sections 1-7 and architecture/questions/prerequisites in parallel')
const out = await parallel([
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + A, { label: 'write:01-plan', phase: 'Write', model: 'haiku' }),
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + B, { label: 'write:09b-14-15', phase: 'Write', model: 'haiku' }),
])
return { fragments: out }

fragments:
**Fragment:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/01-plan.md`

**Size:** 197 lines (budget 280), 52,721 bytes. The seven tables have consistent cell counts. No emoji, and no "best", model or vendor words, except the branch name (see contradiction 12).

**Structure:** title, status paragraph, then the seven required sections.
- §1 Bottom line: 10 points, a routes table (first-visit bytes, build bytes, downloads, JS, library, delivery, relaxations) and a terms list.
- §2 Decisions: D-G1 to D-G26, each with OW and O ids, options and costs, the synthesis's recommendation and the default.
- §3 Target picture: 11 layers, with kind, source, builder, bytes, state words and legend.
- §4 Evidence rules: 17 bullets.
- §5 Workstreams W0 to W21, plus the main-architecture map and parallax.
- §6 Phases: synthesis P0 to P6 and PG, design D phases 0 to 5, and the tests and CI each needs.
- §7 Risks: 15, ranked, each with mitigation and evidence.

**Evidence files cited (31 JSON):** design-d, design-synthesis-website, design-c, mrms, gibs, goes-aws, terrain, radar-tiles, base-imagery, labels-on-globe, design-references, globe-libs, webgl-runtime, google-terms, montana-imagery-buildings, app-integration, prior-work, judge2-rules, judge2-engineering, judge2-product, hosting-options, pipeline-options, rendering-options, rights-matrix, evaluation-predeclared, parallax, main-architecture, prototype-globe, prototype-integration, prototype-mrms, prototype-goes.
- Review key present (14): gibs, goes-aws, mrms, terrain, radar-tiles, base-imagery, labels-on-globe, design-references, globe-libs, webgl-runtime, google-terms, montana-imagery-buildings, app-integration, prior-work.
- Unreviewed (the rest): the designs, syntheses, judges (scores, not fact reviews), hosting, pipeline, rendering, rights, evaluation, parallax, main-architecture and the prototype files. The fragment marks these where it matters.

Repo lines cited were spot-checked: `website.yml`, `test_site.py:459-471`, `base.html:45`, `DESIGN.md:167-168`, `ROADMAP.md` 35–48 and 89, `DECISIONS.md` 310–312 and 359–361, `prototype/globe.js:293-297`. No live source was re-fetched.

**Contradictions found, and how the fragment handles them**
1. GIBS latency: the brief says 30–96 min. gibs.json (reviewed) says 19–45 min typical, late frames 76–96 min. The fragment uses the reviewed figures.
2. MSL imagery: the brief says "retiring 2026-07-31". The reviewed file says the old host retired on that date (already past), and the replacement answered 200 on 2026-10-17.
3. Site-files rule ID: the brief and design D call it D-G1, but D-G1 is the library decision in the original plan and the synthesis (OW-1). The fragment uses D-G15 (OW-15) and notes design D's label.
4. "No echo is not clear": main-architecture.json point 7 says it must match DESIGN.md:275-276, but that text reads "Missing is not dry". The phrase is not in the repo. The fragment marks it as proposed.
5. design-d.json's download total (56.6–60.7 MB) omits the Band 13 file (3.9 MB per step, goes-aws.json). The corrected figure is 60.5–64.6 MB, computed. The fragment uses the corrected figure.
6. design-c.json's P1–P6 numbering differs from the synthesis's P1–P6 and PG (its P5 is the desktop-era globe). The fragment uses the synthesis's numbering.
7. Phones for the globe gate: the synthesis PG requires two, design D phase 5 requires three.
8. Design C first visit: 0.85 MB in the synthesis versus 0.95 MB in judge2-engineering K6 (which uses design C's 0.66 MB budget). The Map today is 0.28 MB (synthesis) versus 0.29 MB (judge2-engineering K6).
9. Scheduled-run gaps: the synthesis has four starts with median 151.5 min (05:13Z). judge2-engineering has three with median 146.5 min (04:46Z). The fragment uses the later figure.
10. Stale ROADMAP references: the plan critiques cite ROADMAP:11 and :39 for the baseline. The current file has these at lines 46–48 and 89. DESIGN.md:29 says 320 px while `smoke_pages.py:23` tests 288 px; both are shown.
11. The freeze of Map and Now is cited to ROADMAP.md:40–43 in the synthesis. That roadmap text only names the feedback week, so the fragment labels the freeze as the synthesis's proposal (OW-8).
12. The branch name `codex/montana-weather-pilot` carries an AI-vendor word, which conflicts with the no-vendor-identifier rule. The brief requires the name, so it is kept. prototype-integration.json deliberately omits it.
13. GOES-East longitude: §8 gives a 0.14 km shift and §9 says the 15 km bound moves to about 34 km. These agree once rounded, but the 33 km legend bound may need to read 34 km. Flagged in D-G26.
14. The 217 GB/month loop figure and the 43 GB/month figure both assume 4,320 builds (10-minute cadence). Measured runs do not meet that cadence.
15. Prototype review flag F1 (dBZ colour steps in the browser) is fixed in the current `globe.js` (lines 293–297), but prototype-integration.json's fixes list does not record it.

Wrote the three fragments. Each one is within its line budget, every evidence link resolves, and README.md was not touched.

**Fragments (absolute paths)**
- `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/09b-architecture.md`: 170 lines (budget 170); 48 evidence links.
- `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/14-questions.md`: 91 lines (budget 100); 63 question rows, grouped as specified; 15 links.
- `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-sections/15-prerequisites.md`: 23 lines (budget 50); 17 rows; 2 links.

No model or vendor names, no emoji, and no "best". Repo statements (grep) were checked against the checkout, not main, and no browser check was run.

**Evidence files cited**
- Reviewed (has a `review` key): mrms.json, goes-aws.json, gibs.json, globe-libs.json, terrain.json.
- Unreviewed (no `review` key; cited with that caveat): main-architecture.json, design-synthesis-website.json, design-d.json, design-a.json, design-b.json, design-c.json, judge2-rules.json, judge2-engineering.json, judge2-product.json, parallax.json, evaluation-predeclared.json, hosting-options.json, pipeline-options.json, prototype-goes.json, prototype-globe.json, prototype-mrms.json.
- Scratchpad only, not in the repo: plan-critique-product.json, plan-critique-technical.json.
- Also cross-referenced: the existing fragments 08, 09a and 10; README §1–7.

**Contradictions found**
1. The brief's "no echo is not clear (DESIGN.md:275-276)": DESIGN.md:275-276 says "Missing is not dry". The phrase appears only in plan §4 and design D's legend.
2. D-G1 is used for two questions: the plan §2 library question and design D's streamed-hosts question. §14 uses OW-1 and OW-15.
3. Radar staleness: DESIGN.md:154 and DECISIONS.md:341 say 15 min; gridded.py:53, sources.py:115 and DESIGN.md:333 say 30 min.
4. Phone floor: DESIGN.md:29 says 320 px; DESIGN.md:39 and smoke_pages.py:23 use 288 px.
5. Brief's "AWS GOES ~2–3 min": the Band 13 median is 30 s (goes-aws.json). Only the ACHA and CODC medians (1.9–2.5 min) fit. Brief's "GIBS ~40 min": fits GeoColor only; Band 13 is 19–35 min (gibs.json).
6. Design D's first visit: 2.8 MB is raw bytes (design-d s3). Wire bytes are 1.09 MB with Earth and 0.69 MB without (computed; the synthesis's figure). judge2-engineering K6 gives 1.1 MB.
7. Design D's per-build download (56.6–60.7 MB) omits the 3.9 MB Band 13 object; corrected to 60.5–64.6 MB (computed).
8. Schedule median: 146.5 min (judge2-engineering K1, two gaps) vs 151.5 min (synthesis, three gaps including a 264.5 min gap).
9. MapLibre 6.14.0 bytes: 1,078,892 B (design-c, one file) vs 1,587,206 B (globe-libs, module plus worker). Different file sets.
10. Supervisor log says the 0.5 km MRMS level is underground "over most of Montana"; design-d says that share is unverified. It is unmeasured; the P0 gate measures it.
11. Folium claim: DECISIONS.md:196 (checked); the technical critique cites :188.
12. plan-critique-product cites ROADMAP.md:107 for crew computers. That line is the towns question.
13. "About 2,100 lines" for map.js: ROADMAP.md:25 (main-architecture) vs ROADMAP.md:60-61 (synthesis).
14. plan-critique-technical.json has no `questions_for_the_owner` key. Its owner-level items are mapped in §14.
15. Pilot size for comprehension: 20 (evaluation-predeclared), two (ROADMAP Next 2), five (DESIGN.md:35, per judge2-product; not re-read).
16. The evaluation asks for retrieved time (Q2); map.html and map.js show none (grep).
17. The rule says DEMO (AGENTS.md rule 5); the site says SAMPLE (base.html:16-18, map.html:45-46).
18. The map shows two radar-gap phrases: "No radar coverage" (map.js:34) and "No radar data on this map" (map.js:36). sources.py:116-117 defines negative values as no coverage.
